title: [BUG] SuperOffload Fails when having more than one optimizer group
author: Mahmoud363

comments.author: xylian86
comments.body: @Mahmoud363 Thank you for raising this issue. I’m working on it and will open a PR to address it.

comments.author: xylian86
comments.body:
@Mahmoud363 I have opened a PR (https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/pull/7906) to address it. Could you please test it on your side with this version?

Also, could you share your use case for SuperOffload? For example, are you using it for pre-training, fine-tuning, or just benchmarking?

comments.author: Mahmoud363
comments.body:
@xylian86 Thanks for your fast response.
I am mainly trying it now for benchmarking and will later use it for finetuning.

When I try the PR, it gives me this error:
```
[rank3]:   File "../python3.12/site-packages/deepspeed/runtime/superoffload/superoffload_stage3.py", line 208, in partition_grads
[rank3]:     fp32_grad_tensor.copy_(concatenated_buffer, non_blocking=True)
[rank3]: RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (130280) must match the size of tensor b (129704) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

I think this is because in the code, when multiple parameters belong to the same sub-group, their grad partitions are placed at specific offsets within the flat buffer (fp32_param.grad) and these offsets aren't necessarily contiguous.

Not sure if this is the intended behaviour and it's an issue with my config or it's another thing that requires modifying.

this is the full trace. I don't remember why the line pointed to the wrong one earlier but this is the output with the current PR.

For this run, I mainly tried changing the sub_group_size but the same persists with 1e9.
```
    "zero_optimization": {
        "stage": 3,
        "overlap_comm": false,
        "reduce_bucket_size": 4e8,
        "sub_group_size": 4e8,
        "offload_optimizer": {
            "device": "cpu",
            "pin_memory": true,
            "ratio": 0.90,
            "super_offload": true,
            "cpuadam_cores_perc": 0.90
        }
    },
```

Regarding reproducing. Apologies for not mentioning it earlier but i am specifically running the llava repo finetuning script (https://github.com/LLaVA-VL/LLaVA-NeXT/blob/main/scripts/video/train/SO400M_Qwen2_7B_ov_to_video_am9.sh) with only one learning rate for the whole model (vision tower and mlp adapter learning rate are disabled) while modifying the zero config file

Given that it is a multimodal scenario, the partions in the sub_group may not be contiguous  compared to the case of Qwen3-4B. 


To overcome this point, i applied a monkey patch to this function as follows to copy each gradient separately:
```
    @instrument_w_nvtx
    def partition_grads(self, params_to_release: List[Parameter], grad_partitions: List[Tensor]) -> None:
        # FIX: Track per-partition offsets instead of min/max span.
        # Original used buffer_numel_min/max to narrow a contiguous span, but
        # padding gaps between parameters made the span larger than the
        # concatenated data, causing a size mismatch RuntimeError.
        grad_info_by_subgroup = {}  # i -> [(dest_offset, grad_partition), ...]

        for param, grad_partition in zip(params_to_release, grad_partitions):
            i, dest_offset, _ = self.grad_position[self.get_param_id(param)]

            if self.is_gradient_accumulation_boundary:
                self.norm_for_param_grads[self.get_param_id(param)] = self._constant_buffered_norm2(grad_partition)

            if i not in grad_info_by_subgroup:
                grad_info_by_subgroup[i] = []
            grad_info_by_subgroup[i].append((dest_offset, grad_partition))

        if self.is_gradient_accumulation_boundary:
            for i, grad_infos in grad_info_by_subgroup.items():
                fp32_grad = self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[i].grad

                if self.subgroup_to_device[i] == 'cpu':
                    param_group_id = self.sub_group_to_group_id[i]
                    fp32_param = self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[i]

                    # FIX: Copy each partition to its exact offset (handles gaps)
                    # Original: fp32_grad_tensor = narrow(min, max-min)  ← includes gaps
                    #           concatenated_buffer = cat(partitions)    ← no gaps
                    #           fp32_grad_tensor.copy_(concatenated_buffer) ← SIZE MISMATCH
                    for dest_offset, grad_partition in grad_infos:
                        fp32_grad.narrow(0, dest_offset, grad_partition.numel()).copy_(
                            grad_partition.to(dtype=self.master_weights_and_grads_dtype), non_blocking=True)

                    # FIX: Send full flat grad (same size as fp32_param.data) to worker
                    # Original sent concatenated_buffer.data which was smaller
                    self.superoffload_cpu_optimizer.async_step(param_group_id, i, fp32_param.data,
                                                               fp32_param.grad.data)
                    self.async_cpuadam_num += 1

                    result = self.superoffload_cpu_optimizer.get_result()
                    if result is not None:
                        self._reassign_or_swap_out_partitioned_parameters_async(result[TaskKeys.SUB_GROUP_ID],
                                                                                result[ResultKeys.UPDATED_PARAM])
                        self.async_cpuadam_num -= 1

                else:
                    # FIX: Same per-partition copy for non-CPU subgroups
                    for dest_offset, grad_partition in grad_infos:
                        fp32_grad.narrow(0, dest_offset, grad_partition.numel()).copy_(
                            grad_partition.to(dtype=self.master_weights_and_grads_dtype), non_blocking=True)

        # Clean up parameter gradients
        for param in params_to_release:
            if not get_accelerator().is_synchronized_device():
                param.grad.record_stream(get_accelerator().current_stream())
            param.grad = None
```

This works for the 7B case but not sure if there is a better way to handle it.

could this have to with section 4.4 of the paper regarding:
"gradient clipping and normalization are deferred to occur during CPU idle periods, concurrent with the GPU executing the forward pass for the next iteration. "

If gradient clipping is triggered on the first step and gradients aren't ready, could it be causing this issue?  
I am not sure if this is the normal behavior and the issue is why the gradients are not ready by that point or something else is causing it.

comments.author: Mahmoud363
comments.body:
The rollback issue is due to gradient clipping being triggered at the first step which is expected to fail as there is no state to revert to. 
If I disable the gradient clipping, I get the following issue with a duplicated parameter in one of the buckets:
Debug output:
```
[15:26:57.012849] [DEBUG] Duplicate ds_id=505, param_name=model.layers.4.mlp.up_proj.weight, grad is None: False, bucket size: 43
```
Error:
```
[rank1]:   File "env/lib/python3.12/site-packages/deepspeed/utils/nvtx.py", line 20, in wrapped_fn
[rank1]:     ret_val = func(*args, **kwargs)

[rank1]:     assert len(set(p.ds_id for p in params_in_bucket)) == len(params_in_bucket), f'{len(set(p.ds_id for p in params_in_bucket))}, {len(params_in_bucket)}'
```

From my debugging, it seems that the issue comes from reduce_independent_p_g_buckets_and_remove_grads but I haven't been able to fully understand why it is the case.

This is obtained when running the LLaVA video script with the base LLM being Qwen2-7B and the ViT being Siglip. The projector is initialized from scratch and the rest of the model isn't aligned with visual modality yet, so it explains the gradient clipping being triggered.
